answer: An agent economy can limit influence by requiring every account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit bids, with voting weight capped per deposit and slashed when a challenge proves fraud. A sybil operator can still create many names, but each useful identity ties up real capital; splitting funds among accounts does not multiply their total weight. Like a basalt marker beside a glacier lagoon, the deposit makes identities costly to move or replace, while honest agents recover it after valid participation.
